defect: resolve_invocation_assertion calls union_comparator::is_contained_by(codebase, asserted_type, &resolved_assertion_type, ...) to decide whether an invocation type assertion is always_redundant, without checking whether resolved_assertion_type contains a template parameter. Because union_comparator::is_contained_by and atomic_comparator::is_contained_by treat concrete types as contained by a TAtomic::GenericParameter when its upper bound accepts them (e.g., array-key into T of array-key, null into T of ?string, or any type into T of mixed), narrowing a concrete value to a template type T is falsely reported as RedundantTypeComparison.
trigger: A generic method or function annotated with `@template T of array-key` and `@assert T $value` (or `@psalm-assert T $value`) called with `$value` of concrete type `array-key` (or `@template T` of `mixed` called with any concrete type like `string`).
match_rule: Identify that resolve_invocation_assertion treats an assertion to a template/generic parameter type (resolved_assertion_type containing a GenericParameter/template) as redundant because is_contained_by succeeds against the template's upper-bound constraint (e.g., array-key <= T of array-key or T of mixed), producing a false-positive RedundantTypeComparison.
near_misses: Complaining generally about is_contained_by ignoring variance or flags, or about always_redundant handling of mixed asserted_type or negated assertions without identifying template/generic target types.
why_findable: The diff adds the is_contained_by check in post_process.rs right next to !asserted_type.is_mixed(), while union_comparator::is_contained_by and atomic_comparator::is_contained_by in crates/codex/src/ttype/comparator/ explicitly return true when a concrete input satisfies a container GenericParameter's constraint (ArrayKey against T of array-key, Null against nullable T, or any type against is_templated_as_vanilla_mixed).
notes: Fix commit 5f58e947 adds `!resolved_assertion_type.has_template()` and regression test assert_concrete_to_template_type.php.

defect: resolve_method_from_classname unconditionally checks for `__callStatic` (and resolve_method_from_metadata passes `is_static = true` to report_magic_call_without_call_method) for all calls routed through the static method resolver, including `parent::foo()`. In PHP, `parent::foo()` from an instance context forwards to the parent's instance `__call` magic method rather than `__callStatic`, and resolve_method_from_metadata already treats `classname.is_parent()` as an instance call on `$this`.
trigger: A subclass calling `parent::pseudoMethod()` where the parent class defines `__call` (and `@method void pseudoMethod(...)` or an undocumented magic method) without defining `__callStatic`.
match_rule: Identify that `parent::` calls routed through static_method.rs check `__callStatic` instead of `__call` (and report MissingMagicMethod for `__callStatic` / NonExistentMethod instead of accepting `__call`), despite PHP dispatching `parent::` magic calls to `__call` and `classname.is_parent()` already being distinguished.
near_misses: Flagging general static-vs-instance method resolution, visibility checks, or `$obj::foo()` without specifically identifying `parent::` checking `__callStatic` instead of `__call`.
why_findable: In the diff, resolve_method_from_classname hardcodes `atom("__callStatic")` and passes `is_static = true` to report_magic_call_without_call_method, while resolve_method_from_metadata in the same file (line 322) explicitly branches on `classname.is_parent()` (defined in resolver/class_name.rs) to treat `parent::` calls as instance calls.
notes: base_commit is c76795c30^ because the bug spans the consecutive two-commit series on 2025-09-14 (c76795c30 adding `@method` support with hardcoded `__callStatic`, immediately followed by dc333edb26 adding MissingMagicMethod validation on top of it).

defect: 9bdc4c0786 changed the `get_right_parenthesis` closure to call `format_token(f, argument_list.right_parenthesis, ")")` and `f.print_dangling_comments(...)`, which mutate FormatterState by consuming comments attached to the `)` token. However, `should_expand_first` (and `should_expand_last` via `all_arguments_broken_out(f)`) invokes `get_right_parenthesis(f, ...)` in both alternatives of `Group::conditional`, so the first branch consumes the trailing/dangling comments on `)` and leaves the fallback `all_arguments_broken_out(f)` branch without them; when the printer selects the fallback branch, comments after `)` are silently lost.
trigger: Formatting a two-argument call where the first argument is expandable/multiline and there is a trailing comment on the closing parenthesis, e.g. `foo('\n', [$a]); // Comment`.
match_rule: Identify that `get_right_parenthesis` (calling `format_token` / `print_dangling_comments`, which consume comments from FormatterState) is called multiple times across branches of `Group::conditional` (e.g., inline branch and `all_arguments_broken_out`), causing comments attached to the closing `)` to be consumed on the first call and lost when the second branch is printed.
near_misses: Complaining about `print_dangling_comments` spacing or unrelated inlining heuristics in `should_inline_breaking_arguments` without identifying duplicate stateful consumption of closing-parenthesis comments across conditional branches.
why_findable: The diff changes `get_right_parenthesis` from emitting `Document::String(")")` to calling `format_token(f, argument_list.right_parenthesis, ")")` (defined in internal/format/mod.rs as calling `print_leading_comments` and `print_trailing_comments`), while calling `get_right_parenthesis(f, ...)` in both `Group::conditional` branches (`should_expand_first` calls `get_right_parenthesis` directly and then `all_arguments_broken_out(f)` which calls it again).
notes: Directly tested by issue_294.

defect: 9110b3faed added `CodebaseMetadata::get_method_visibility(class, method)` and switched `check_method_visibility` to call it, introducing two cross-site visibility defects: (1) its fallback looks up `(lowercase_class, lowercase_method)` directly in `self.function_likes` without resolving the declaring class via `get_declaring_method_class`, so for any inherited or trait method without a `trait_visibility_map` entry it returns `None` and `check_method_visibility` silently returns `true` (bypassing private/protected visibility checks); (2) it looks up `lowercase_method` in `trait_visibility_map`, which `scanner/class_like.rs` keys by the original trait method name rather than the alias, so aliasing `setInactive as private parentSetInactive` while declaring `public function setInactive()` falsely applies `private` visibility to the class's own public `setInactive()`.
trigger: Either calling an inherited protected/private method on a subclass from outside the class (silently allowed), or declaring `use T { foo as private bar; }` alongside `public function foo()` and calling `$obj->foo()` (falsely rejected as invalid-method-access).
match_rule: Identify either (a) that `get_method_visibility` looks up `(lowercase_class, lowercase_method)` directly in `function_likes` without resolving the declaring class, causing `None` -> `check_method_visibility` returning `true` for inherited/trait methods, or (b) that `trait_visibility_map` lookup in `get_method_visibility` collides with a class's own method when a trait method is aliased with changed visibility because `scanner/class_like.rs` keys `trait_visibility_map` by original method name instead of alias.
near_misses: Complaining about `self` return type replacement in `invocation/resolver.rs` or case sensitivity of class names without identifying the missing declaring-class resolution or trait alias visibility key collision.
why_findable: In `visibility/mod.rs` right above the changed line, `check_method_visibility` already had to call `get_declaring_method_identifier` before looking up `function_likes`, whereas the newly added `get_method_visibility` skips declaring-class lookup and returns `Option` that `check_method_visibility` turns into `return true`. Likewise, `scanner/class_like.rs` visibly inserts `trait_visibility_map` under `method_name` rather than `alias`.
notes: Fix commit af8999c6 fixes both `get_method_visibility` declaring-class lookup and `trait_visibility_map` alias keying/call-site lookup.

defect: The `parse_url` plugin models the `path` key in `get_full_array_return_type` as always present (`(false, get_string())`) and models `PHP_URL_PATH` as `null|string`. In PHP, `parse_url('https://example.com')` omits the `'path'` key entirely when there is no path, and whenever `'path'` is present it is a `non-empty-string`.
trigger: Analyzing `parse_url($url)['path']` or `parse_url($url, PHP_URL_PATH)` on a URL without a path such as `'https://example.com'`.
match_rule: Identify that `parse_url.rs` marks the `'path'` array key as non-optional (`false`) instead of optional (`true`) and/or gives `path`/`PHP_URL_PATH` type `string` instead of `non-empty-string`.
near_misses: Complaining about `port` integer bounds or other URL components without identifying the `'path'` optionality / non-empty-string bug.
why_findable: Visible directly in `parse_url.rs` where `'path'` is the sole component inserted with `false` (required) and `get_string()` instead of `true` (optional) and `get_non_empty_string()`.
notes: Local stdlib type-model bug inside parse_url.rs (`relation: false`).

defect: In `unary_node_needs_parens`, non-`!` `UnaryPrefix` nodes (including casts like `(string) $b`) are assigned `Precedence::IncDec` — which `crates/syntax/src/token/mod.rs` defines with LOWER precedence than `Concat`, `AddSub`, `Comparison`, etc. — and RHS unary expressions are only skipped via the strict inequality `if e.operator.span().end < unary_span.start { return false; }`. Because `Span` is half-open `[start, end)`, when there is no space between the binary operator and the unary cast (`'='.(string)$b`), `end == start`, so the strict `<` guard fails and `Precedence::IncDec < Precedence::Concat` evaluates to `true`, spuriously wrapping the cast in redundant parentheses (`'=' . ((string) $b)`) and breaking formatter idempotency.
trigger: Formatting `'='.(string)$b` (a unary cast immediately following a binary operator with no intervening whitespace).
match_rule: Identify that `e.operator.span().end < unary_span.start` (strict `<` instead of `<=`) fails when a binary operator and RHS unary expression are adjacent without whitespace (where half-open `end == start`), causing `unary_node_needs_parens` to fall through to `precedence < parent_precedence` (where `Precedence::IncDec` is ordered below binary operators like `Concat`) and spuriously parenthesize casts/unary expressions.
near_misses: Commenting only on error-control `@` handling or binary associativity without identifying the strict `<` span boundary check or `Precedence::IncDec` ordering for RHS unary expressions.
why_findable: The diff introduces both `Precedence::IncDec` for `UnaryPrefix` and `if e.operator.span().end < unary_span.start { return false; }` in `parens.rs`; inspecting `Precedence` in `crates/syntax/src/token/mod.rs` shows `IncDec` sits below `Assignment`/`Concat`/`AddSub`, and `mago-span` uses half-open `[start, end)` offsets so adjacent tokens satisfy `end == start`.
notes: Directly tested by issue_298.

defect: The `opening_tag_on_own_line` check suppresses the newline after `<?php` whenever `f.source_text.contains("?>")`. However, `ClosingTag::format` in `crates/formatter/src/internal/format/mod.rs` strips redundant trailing `?>` closing tags at EOF. On pass 1 of `<?php echo 1; ?>`, `f.source_text` contains `?>` so the opening tag stays inline while `ClosingTag::format` removes `?>` (`<?php echo 1;`); on pass 2, `f.source_text` no longer contains `?>` so `opening_tag_on_own_line` triggers and moves `echo 1;` onto a new line, violating formatter idempotency (and also false-matching `?>` inside strings/comments).
trigger: Formatting a PHP-only file with statements on the opening-tag line and a trailing closing tag, e.g. `<?php echo 1; ?>`, with `opening_tag_on_own_line: true` (the default).
match_rule: Identify that checking raw `!f.source_text.contains("?>")` in `should_add_new_line_or_space_after_stmt` breaks idempotency when the formatter strips a redundant trailing `?>` closing tag (or falsely matches `?>` in strings/comments instead of inspecting AST inline HTML/closing tags).
near_misses: Complaining about preset defaults (`opening_tag_on_own_line: true`) or `empty_line_after_opening_tag` without identifying the raw `f.source_text.contains("?>")` check interacting with trailing `?>` removal or non-tag `?>` occurrences.
why_findable: The diff adds `!f.source_text.contains("?>")` in `statement.rs`, while `ClosingTag::format` in `crates/formatter/src/internal/format/mod.rs` (lines 285-299) visibly omits trailing `?>` tags, immediately creating a pass-1 vs pass-2 divergence on `<?php echo 1; ?>`.
notes: Directly tested by inline_php_closing_tag_idempotency and issue_1350.

defect: In `crates/analyzer/src/assertion.rs`, `scrape_special_function_call_assertions` emits `Assertion::IsType(TObject::HasMethod(...))` / `HasProperty(...)` for `method_exists($target, 'm')` and `property_exists($target, 'p')` regardless of whether `$target` is an object or a class-name string. However, the consumers `reconcile_has_method` and `reconcile_has_property` in `simple_assertion_reconciler.rs` only retain `TAtomic::Object(_)`, `Variable`, `GenericParameter`, and `Mixed`, dropping `TScalar::String(_)` and `TScalar::ClassLikeString(_)` in the `_ =>` arm; consequently, calling `method_exists($className, 'foo')` on a `string` narrows `$className` to `never` instead of `class-string` and emits false impossible-condition errors.
trigger: Guarding a static method call on a string class name with `if (method_exists($className, 'someMethod')) { $className::someMethod(); }` where `$className` has type `string`.
match_rule: Identify that `assertion.rs` emits `HasMethod`/`HasProperty` assertions for `method_exists()`/`property_exists()` on any first argument (including `string`/`class-string`), while `reconcile_has_method` and `reconcile_has_property` drop `String`/`ClassLikeString` atomics to `never` instead of narrowing them to `class-string`.
near_misses: Complaining about `function_exists()`/`defined()` tracking or `trust_existence_checks` config defaults without identifying that `method_exists`/`property_exists` accepts `string`/`class-string` and gets dropped during reconciliation.
why_findable: The diff adds both the assertion producer in `assertion.rs` (unconditionally scraping `method_exists`/`property_exists` arg 0 as `TObject::HasMethod`/`HasProperty`) and the reconcilers `reconcile_has_method`/`reconcile_has_property` in `simple_assertion_reconciler.rs` whose match lacks `TScalar::String(_) | TScalar::ClassLikeString(_)`, falling into `_ => { did_remove_type = true; }`.
notes: Directly tested by issue_1374.

defect: In the `is_single_late_breaking_argument` branch of `print_argument_list`, the `break_contents` arm of `Document::IfBreak` wraps the argument in a new inner `Document::Group` containing `Document::Line(Line::default())` and an unconditional `Document::String(",")` (not wrapped in `IfBreak`). When the enclosing expression breaks (selecting `break_contents`) but the inner `Group` still fits on one line, `Line::default()` collapses to an unwanted space after `(` and before `)` and the trailing comma is printed on a single line (`unique( fn(...) => ..., )`).
trigger: Formatting a broken method chain ending in a single short arrow-function argument that fits on one line, e.g. `collect([...])->unique(fn($x) => $x->foo())` with `trailing_comma: true`.
match_rule: Identify that in `is_single_late_breaking_argument`, the `IfBreak` break branch uses `Line::default()` (collapsing to spaces when its inner `Group` stays flat) and/or emits an unconditional `","` instead of wrapping it in `IfBreak` (producing spaces inside parens and an inline trailing comma).
near_misses: Complaining about the duplicate `has_comment` call in `argument_has_surrounding_comments` or `is_simple_expression` heuristics without identifying `Line::default()` or the unconditional trailing comma in `is_single_late_breaking_argument`.
why_findable: In the same function in `call_arguments.rs`, the regular argument list uses `Line::soft()` and `Document::IfBreak(IfBreak::then(Document::String(",")))`, whereas the newly added `is_single_late_breaking_argument` branch wraps `Line::default()` and plain `Document::String(",")` inside a fresh `Document::Group`.
notes: Local to `print_argument_list` in `call_arguments.rs` (`relation: false`). Directly tested by issue_317.

defect: ce96523d5b removed the sealed-hierarchy pre-check in `simple_negated_assertion_reconciler::reconcile` and unconditionally returned `Some(subtract_object(...))` for every `TAtomic::Object(TObject::Named(_))`. Because its caller `negated_assertion_reconciler::reconcile` returns immediately whenever `simple_negated_assertion_reconciler::reconcile` returns `Some(...)` (skipping the complex inheritance/interface subtraction path), and `subtract_object` only handles exact name equality and sealed `permitted_inheritors`, non-sealed subclass/interface subtractions (e.g., `!($x instanceof SomeInterface)` when `$x` is a class implementing `SomeInterface`) are never subtracted, causing broken type narrowing and false positives.
trigger: Negated `instanceof` check against a non-sealed interface or parent class on a variable typed as a concrete implementing/extending class (or union containing it), e.g., `if ($obj instanceof FooInterface) { ... } else { ... }`.
match_rule: Identify that unconditionally returning `Some(subtract_object(...))` for `TAtomic::Object(TObject::Named(_))` in `simple_negated_assertion_reconciler::reconcile` short-circuits the caller (`negated_assertion_reconciler::reconcile`) and bypasses general/complex object inheritance and interface subtraction for non-sealed hierarchies.
near_misses: Complaining about performance of `permitted_inheritors` lookup or case sensitivity without identifying that non-sealed object hierarchies are intercepted by `Some(subtract_object(...))` and bypass `negated_assertion_reconciler`.
why_findable: The diff explicitly removes the guard that fell through (`None`) to `negated_assertion_reconciler::reconcile` for non-sealed classes and unconditionally returns `Some(subtract_object(...))`, while `subtract_object` in the same file only checks `permitted_inheritors` and exact class name equality rather than general `is_instance_of` / interface relationships.
notes: Fix commit 2984e2a4 explicitly cites ce96523d5b as the introducing commit and adds test `subtract_objects.php`.

defect: c7d46a1e07 introduced `instantiation_needs_parens` to honor PHP 8.4's `NewWithoutParentheses` and `parentheses_around_new_in_member_access`, but only called it in the `Node::Call` branch (and `member_access.rs`), leaving `Node::ClosureCreation` (later `PartialApplication`), `Node::ArrayAccess`, and `Node::Access` to call `callee_expression_need_parenthesis`, which unconditionally returns `true` for `Expression::Instantiation`. As a result, `new Foo()->bar(...)` (first-class callable / partial application), `new Foo()->prop`, and `new Foo()[0]` are still forced into unnecessary parentheses on PHP 8.4+.
trigger: Formatting `new Foo()->bar(...)` (method closure creation / partial application) or `new Foo()[0]` on PHP 8.4+ with `parentheses_around_new_in_member_access: false`.
match_rule: Identify that `instantiation_needs_parens` is only invoked in the `Node::Call` branch (and not in `callee_expression_need_parenthesis` or the `ClosureCreation`/`Access`/`ArrayAccess` branches), causing `Expression::Instantiation` to always be parenthesized in those member/callable/array access contexts even when PHP 8.4 allows omitting parens.
near_misses: Complaining about `parentheses_in_new_expression` when there are no arguments without identifying the missing `instantiation_needs_parens` check for non-`Node::Call` contexts.
why_findable: In `parens.rs`, `called_or_accessed_node_needs_parenthesis` handles `ClosureCreation`, `Call`, `ArrayAccess`, and `Access` consecutively within 40 lines, calling `instantiation_needs_parens` only for `Call` while delegating the others to `callee_expression_need_parenthesis` which excludes `Expression::Instantiation`.
notes: Local to `crates/formatter/src/parens.rs` (`relation: false`).

defect: To preserve explicit specific parameter types on closures over looser inferred types, `add_parameter_types_to_context` sets `declared_type_is_specific = union.is_list() || (!union.is_mixed() && !union.is_vanilla_mixed() && !union.is_array())`, assuming `TUnion::is_array()` only matches bare `array`. However, `TUnion::is_array()` in `crates/codex/src/ttype/union.rs` returns `true` for ALL `TAtomic::Array(_)` types, including specific docblock array shapes (`array{id: Foo}`) and typed generic arrays (`array<string, int>`). Consequently, `declared_type_is_specific` is `false` for docblock array shapes, causing inferred closure parameter types (e.g. `mixed` or untyped `array`) to overwrite the explicit docblock shape.
trigger: Passing a closure annotated with `/** @param array{id: Foo} $data */ function (array $data): Foo { return $data['id']; }` to a function expecting untyped `Closure` or a generic callable.
match_rule: Identify that `!union.is_array()` in `add_parameter_types_to_context` evaluates to `false` for specific array types (such as keyed array shapes `array{...}` or generic `array<K, V>`) because `TUnion::is_array()` matches all `TAtomic::Array` variants rather than only bare/vanilla `array`, causing explicit docblock array shapes on closure parameters to be overwritten by inferred types.
near_misses: Complaining about `is_mixed()` vs `is_vanilla_mixed()` or string callable handling in the same commit without identifying that `union.is_array()` matches shaped/typed arrays and causes `declared_type_is_specific` to be false.
why_findable: The diff adds `union.is_list() || (... && !union.is_array())` in `statement/function_like/mod.rs`, while `TUnion::is_array()` in `crates/codex/src/ttype/union.rs` (line 765) visibly returns `self.types.iter().all(|t| t.is_array())`, which is true for keyed shapes and generic arrays alike.
notes: Directly tested by issue_806.

defect: e294ce2a48 added `PropertyHookMetadata` (`parameter` and `return_type_metadata`) in `crates/codex/src/metadata/property_hook.rs`, scanned them in `crates/codex/src/scanner/property.rs` (producing unpopulated `TObject::Named` references for enums and class-likes), and validated them against property types in the analyzer — but never updated `populate_class_like_types` in `crates/codex/src/populator/hierarchy.rs` to call `populate_union_type` on `property_metadata.hooks`. Because the property's own type is populated (converting enum `Suit` to `TObject::Enum(Suit)`) while its hook's `set(Suit $value)` parameter remains unpopulated (`TObject::Named(Suit)`), valid enum property hooks fail analysis with spurious type mismatches.
trigger: Declaring a class property typed with a PHP enum and a `set` hook referencing that enum, e.g. `public Suit $suit { get => $this->suit; set(Suit $value) => $value; }`.
match_rule: Identify that `PropertyHookMetadata` parameter and return types scanned in `scanner/property.rs` are never passed through `populate_union_type` in `populator/hierarchy.rs::populate_class_like_types`, leaving enum/symbol types unpopulated (`TObject::Named` instead of `TObject::Enum`, and missing symbol references) when compared against populated property types.
near_misses: Complaining about hook visibility, virtual property detection, or missing hook analysis checks without identifying that hook parameter/return `TypeMetadata` is never populated in the codex populator.
why_findable: The diff adds `hooks: AtomMap<PropertyHookMetadata>` with `return_type_metadata` and `parameter` type metadata on `PropertyMetadata` and scans them in `scanner/property.rs`, while `populator/hierarchy.rs::populate_class_like_types` iterates `metadata.properties.values_mut()` and populates every other type field on `PropertyMetadata` without touching `property_metadata.hooks`.
notes: Directly tested by issue_719.

defect: 738d4e0ade introduced two formatter-printer contract bugs: (1) `DocumentString::format` unconditionally appends `Document::DoNotTrim` to every line including empty lines (`""`), which sets `Printer.can_trim = false` in `printer/mod.rs` and prevents `handle_trim(Trim::Whitespace)` on the following `HardLine` from stripping the printer's own indentation whitespace on blank heredoc/nowdoc lines; (2) `string_width` in `utils.rs` was changed to return `s.lines().map(line_width).max()` instead of the last line's width, corrupting `Printer.pos` (the current column cursor on the final line) after multiline string literals and breaking line-width fitting decisions.
trigger: Formatting either an indented heredoc/nowdoc containing a blank line (leaves trailing indentation spaces on the empty line) or a call containing a multiline string literal followed by another argument (corrupts `Printer.pos` width tracking).
match_rule: Identify either (a) that emitting `Document::DoNotTrim` on empty lines in `DocumentString::format` prevents `Printer::handle_trim` from trimming leading indentation on blank heredoc/nowdoc lines, or (b) that `string_width` returning the max line width across lines instead of the last line's width corrupts the printer's current line column position `self.pos` after multiline strings.
near_misses: Complaining about the Arabic word special case in `line_width` or `could_expand_value` without identifying `DoNotTrim` on empty lines or `string_width` returning max instead of last line width for `Printer.pos`.
why_findable: Both defects are directly visible in the diff together with `Printer` in `crates/formatter/src/internal/printer/mod.rs`: `Printer::handle_trim` skips trimming the preceding indentation whenever `DoNotTrim` was emitted (even after `Document::String("")`), and `Printer` adds `string_width(s)` directly to `self.pos` (which tracks only the current line's column).
notes: Fix commit 137035ac fixes both bugs 3 hours later and updates `issue_164` and adds `psl_regressions`.

defect: The newly added `iterator_to_array` handler passes positional index `0` instead of `1` to `get_argument(invocation.arguments_source, 0, vec!["preserve_keys"])`, reading the `$iterator` argument as `$preserve_keys`, fails to default omitted `$preserve_keys` to `true`, and falls back to `get_mixed()` instead of `get_arraykey()` for keys when `$preserve_keys` is unknown.
trigger: Analyzing `iterator_to_array($iter)` (omitted 2nd arg) or `iterator_to_array($iter, false)` (2nd positional arg ignored because index 0 reads `$iter`).
match_rule: Identify that `get_argument(..., 0, vec!["preserve_keys"])` uses wrong positional index `0` (same as `iterator`) instead of `1`, and/or fails to default omitted `$preserve_keys` to `true`.
near_misses: Complaining about `Iterator<Value>` single-parameter normalization in `builder.rs` without identifying the wrong argument index `0` or missing `true` default for `preserve_keys` in `iterator.rs`.
why_findable: Lines 36 and 48 of the newly created `iterator.rs` sit 12 lines apart and both call `get_argument(invocation.arguments_source, 0, ...)` — one for `preserve_keys` and one for `iterator`.
notes: Local copy-paste typo inside `iterator.rs` (`relation: false`). Directly tested by `iterator_to_array.php`.

defect: 6550fdb1b1 added class-level `@type` / `@phpstan-type` / `@psalm-type` and `@import-type` aliases into `Scanner::file_type_aliases` and `Scanner::file_imported_aliases`, exposing them through `Scanner::get_current_type_resolution_context()`. However, `Scanner::walk_method` still passes `let type_resolution = if method.is_static() { None } else { Some(self.get_current_type_resolution_context()) };` to `scan_method` in `crates/codex/src/scanner/function_like.rs` (to avoid inheriting instance `@template` params). As a result, static methods receive `None` and fail to resolve class type aliases in their `@param`/`@return` docblocks.
trigger: Declaring a class with `@phpstan-type Params = array{host?: string}` and a `public static function connect(array $parameters)` annotated with `@param Params $parameters`.
match_rule: Identify that `Scanner::walk_method` passes `None` for `type_resolution` when `method.is_static()` is true (skipping `get_current_type_resolution_context()`), causing static methods to lose the class's `@type`/`@import-type` aliases when `scan_method` parses their docblocks.
near_misses: Complaining about `file_type_aliases` leaking across classes in the same file without identifying that static methods receive `None` and cannot resolve class type aliases.
why_findable: The diff wires `file_type_aliases` and `file_imported_aliases` into `Scanner::get_current_type_resolution_context()` in `scanner/mod.rs`, while `walk_method` in the same struct explicitly skips calling `get_current_type_resolution_context()` whenever `method.is_static()` is true and passes `None` to `scan_method`.
notes: Directly tested by `type_alias_in_class_method_parameters.php`.

defect: `merge_type_preserving_nullability` is called at scan time from `scanner/function_like.rs` and `scanner/property.rs` (before type expansion) and appends `|null` whenever `real_type` is nullable and `!docblock_type.type_union.accepts_null()`. However, `TUnion::accepts_null()` in `crates/codex/src/ttype/union.rs` only inspects unexpanded atomics and returns `false` for expandable types (`TAtomic::Conditional`, `TAtomic::Alias`, `TAtomic::Derived`, `TAtomic::Reference`). Thus a conditional return like `@return ($x is true ? string : null)` paired with native `: ?string` is corrupted into `($x is true ? string : null)|null`, making callers always see `|null` even when `$x` is `true`.
trigger: A function with a nullable native return type `: ?string` and a conditional docblock return `@return ($flag is true ? string : null)` (or a nullable `@type` alias).
match_rule: Identify that `merge_type_preserving_nullability` calls `accepts_null()` at scan time on unexpanded docblock types (such as conditional return types `TAtomic::Conditional`, type aliases `TAtomic::Alias`, or derived/reference types), where `accepts_null()` returns `false`, causing `as_nullable()` to unconditionally append `|null` and break conditional/aliased return types.
near_misses: Complaining about parameter default `= null` or `is_nullable()` vs `accepts_null()` on `real_type` without identifying that unexpanded/expandable docblock types (conditionals, aliases, etc.) return `false` from `accepts_null()` at scan time.
why_findable: The diff adds `merge_type_preserving_nullability` inside `crates/codex/src/scanner/` (scan phase, before `expander.rs` runs) calling `docblock_type.type_union.accepts_null()`, and inspecting `TUnion::accepts_null()` in `crates/codex/src/ttype/union.rs` immediately shows it returns `false` for `TAtomic::Conditional`, `TAtomic::Alias`, and other expandable variants.
notes: Fixed the same day in 4239fae3 with regression test `conditional_return.php`.

defect: In `scan_class_like`, `docblock.imported_type_aliases` are processed and added to `type_context` at line 978 — AFTER `@template-extends` / `@template-implements` / `@template-use` tags are parsed at lines 550-830. Consequently, any class using an `@import-type` alias inside `@extends Parent<ImportedAlias>` fails to resolve `ImportedAlias` as a type alias.

match_rule: Identify that `scan_class_like` processes `docblock.imported_type_aliases` (adding them to `type_context`) only after parsing `@template-extends`/`@template-implements`/`@template-use`, so imported type aliases cannot be referenced in those tags.
near_misses: Complaining about static methods missing type aliases (a separate bug in `scanner/mod.rs`) without identifying the ordering of `imported_type_aliases` vs `@template-extends`/`@template-implements` in `scan_class_like`.
why_findable: Within `scan_class_like` in `crates/codex/src/scanner/class_like.rs`, the diff adds the `docblock.imported_type_aliases` loop at the bottom of the docblock section after `template_extended_offsets` have already been resolved using `type_context`.
notes: Local ordering bug inside `scan_class_like` (`relation: false`). Shares `intro_commit` 6550fdb1b1 with #55 (not counted toward the 25 distinct relation diffs).

defect: When flushing collected `Statement::Use` nodes before the next statement, `print_statement_sequence` unconditionally emits two `Document::Line(Line::hardline())` even when the last `use` statement is terminated by `Terminator::ClosingTag` (`<?php use Thing ?>`) or immediately followed by `Statement::ClosingTag` (`<?php use Thing; ?>`), inserting extra newlines on every pass and causing non-idempotent formatting.
trigger: Formatting inline PHP templates containing `<?php use Thing; ?>` or `<?php use Thing ?>` followed by HTML/another PHP tag.
match_rule: Identify that flushing `use_statements` in `print_statement_sequence` unconditionally emits hardlines after `print_use_statements` without checking whether the last `use` ends with `Terminator::ClosingTag` or is followed by `Statement::ClosingTag`.
near_misses: Complaining about `sort_uses` or `expand_use_groups` logic without identifying the unconditional hardlines emitted after `use_statements` when terminated/followed by `?>`.
why_findable: Directly below the new `if !use_statements.is_empty()` block in `print_statement_sequence`, the `match stmt` block already special-cases `Terminator::ClosingTag(_)` and `Statement::ClosingTag(_)` to avoid emitting newlines.
notes: Local to `print_statement_sequence` in `statement.rs` (`relation: false`). Directly tested by `issue_297`.

defect: 486b7ca1a5 avoided false `missing-magic-method` errors when `@method` re-documents a real inherited method by checking `let is_pseudo = class_metadata.pseudo_methods.contains(&lowercase_method);` before searching `class_metadata.all_parent_classes` for a real method. However, in `crates/codex/src/scanner/class_like.rs` and `crates/codex/src/populator/`, `ClassLikeMetadata::pseudo_methods` is only populated on the class that wrote the `@method` docblock and is NEVER inherited into child classes. Thus on a subclass `Child extends Parent extends GrandParent` where `Parent` has `@method` and `GrandParent` has the real method, `Child.pseudo_methods` does not contain the method, `is_pseudo` is `false`, `is_inherited` remains `false`, and calling `$child->foo()` falsely reports `missing-magic-method`.
trigger: `GrandParent` defines a real method `getResponse()`, `Parent extends GrandParent` adds `@method stdClass getResponse()`, and `Child extends Parent` calls `(new Child())->getResponse()`.
match_rule: Identify that `class_metadata.pseudo_methods` only contains `@method` tags declared directly on `class_metadata` (not inherited from parent classes by the codex populator), so checking only `class_metadata.pseudo_methods.contains(...)` misses inherited `@method` annotations on a parent class and falsely reports `missing-magic-method` on subclasses.
near_misses: Complaining about `static_pseudo_methods` or `@method` return type inheritance without identifying that `pseudo_methods` is not inherited from parent classes into `class_metadata.pseudo_methods`.
why_findable: The diff adds `class_metadata.pseudo_methods.contains(&lowercase_method)` in `resolver/method.rs` right above a loop over `class_metadata.all_parent_classes`, while `crates/codex/src/` shows `pseudo_methods` is only inserted in `scanner/class_like.rs` and never propagated in `populator/`.
notes: Directly tested by `issue_667.php`.

defect: When refactoring `is_lowercase: bool` to `casing: TStringCasing` in `intersect_string`, the intersection match only preserved `Lowercase` when both sides were `Lowercase` and `Uppercase` when both sides were `Uppercase`, mapping `(Unspecified, Lowercase)` and `(Lowercase, Unspecified)` (and similarly for `Uppercase`) to `TStringCasing::Unspecified`. Thus intersecting `lowercase-string` with `non-empty-string` (or `string` with `lowercase-string`) loses the casing constraint.
trigger: Narrowing a `lowercase-string` (or `uppercase-string`) with a `non-empty-string` check (e.g., `if ($s !== '')`), or narrowing `non-empty-string` with a `lowercase-string` assertion.
match_rule: Identify that the `match (casing, existing_string.casing)` in `intersect_string` drops `Lowercase`/`Uppercase` to `Unspecified` when the other operand is `TStringCasing::Unspecified` (instead of preserving the more specific casing).
near_misses: Complaining about `(Lowercase, Uppercase)` conflict handling or string combiner logic without identifying that `(Unspecified, Lowercase|Uppercase)` / `(Lowercase|Uppercase, Unspecified)` drops casing in `intersect_string`.
why_findable: In the diff itself, the previous line was `is_lowercase || existing_string.is_lowercase` (set intersection of constraints = logical OR), and the replacement match clearly requires BOTH sides to have the casing instead of treating `Unspecified` as the identity element.
notes: Local to `intersect_string` in `simple_assertion_reconciler.rs` (`relation: false`). Directly tested by `issue_1879.php`.

defect: When merging redefined variables across reachable `match` arms, `finalize_context` initializes `final_type = None` and folds `arm_context.locals.get(&var_id)` using `combine_optional_union_types(final_type.as_ref(), arm_type, ...)` without falling back to `self.block_context.locals.get(&var_id)`. Because `combine_optional_union_types(None, None, ...)` in `crates/codex/src/ttype/mod.rs` returns `get_mixed()`, whenever a variable in `all_redefined_vars` is absent from `arm_context.locals` on the first reachable arm (e.g. unset or cleared in that arm while redefined in another), `final_type` immediately becomes `Some(mixed)` and permanently widens the variable to `mixed` after the `match`.
trigger: A `match` expression where a variable (or narrowed property) present in `self.block_context.locals` is absent from the first reachable arm's `locals` (e.g. cleared/unset in arm 1) and redefined in another arm, causing its post-`match` type to collapse to `mixed`.
match_rule: Identify that `finalize_context` in `expression/match.rs` passes `arm_context.locals.get(&var_id)` (without falling back to the pre-match base type) into `combine_optional_union_types`, which returns `mixed` on `(None, None)` when the variable is missing from an arm's `locals`, corrupting the merged variable type to `mixed`.
near_misses: Complaining about `match` exhaustiveness checking or return-type inference without identifying the `combine_optional_union_types` `(None, None) => mixed` / missing base-type fallback when merging `all_redefined_vars` across arms.
why_findable: The diff adds the `all_redefined_vars` loop in `expression/match.rs` calling `combine_optional_union_types(final_type.as_ref(), arm_type, ...)` with initial `final_type = None`, while `combine_optional_union_types` in `crates/codex/src/ttype/mod.rs` (line 468) explicitly returns `get_mixed()` for `(None, None)`.
notes: Directly tested by `issue_2014.php`.

defect: 1f7e2ea5ce added `@require-implements` and `@require-extends` validation in `check_class_like_use` guarded only by `if !class_like_metadata.is_abstract`, requiring `class_like_metadata.all_parent_interfaces.contains(required_interface)`. However, in `crates/codex/src/scanner/class_like.rs` (line 305), `SymbolKind::Trait` leaves `is_abstract = false` (unlike `Interface`) and traits can never implement interfaces (`all_parent_interfaces` is always empty), while `crates/codex/src/populator.rs` never expands `require_implements` / `require_extends` with parent interfaces/classes. Consequently, any trait `D` using trait `C` (`@require-implements A`) — even when `D` declares `@require-implements B` where `B extends A` — is falsely flagged with `MISSING_REQUIRED_INTERFACE`.
trigger: `interface A {}`, `interface B extends A {}`, `/** @require-implements A */ trait C {}`, and `/** @require-implements B */ trait D { use C; }`.
match_rule: Identify that `check_class_like_use` checks `!class_like_metadata.is_abstract` and `all_parent_interfaces.contains(...)` without accounting for traits having `is_abstract == false` (in `scanner/class_like.rs`) and empty `all_parent_interfaces` (or checking inherited `require_implements`/`require_extends` via `populator.rs`), falsely reporting `MISSING_REQUIRED_INTERFACE` / `MISSING_REQUIRED_PARENT` when a trait uses another trait.
near_misses: Complaining about `@mutation-free` or `@inheritors` checks without identifying that traits fail `check_class_like_use`'s `@require-implements`/`@require-extends` validation because `is_abstract` is false for traits and `require_implements` isn't checked/expanded.
why_findable: The diff adds `if !class_like_metadata.is_abstract` around `all_parent_interfaces.contains(required_interface)` inside `check_class_like_use` (which runs on traits too), while `scanner/class_like.rs:305` leaves `is_abstract = false` for `SymbolKind::Trait` and `populator.rs` does not transitively populate `require_implements`.
notes: Directly tested by `require_implements_inherited.php`.

defect: 227f5c07f0 began computing `inferred_return_type` on `TCallable::Signature(signature)` for closures and arrow functions without updating the invocation resolver in `crates/analyzer/src/expression/call/function_call.rs` (which, when invoking a `TCallable::Signature` that has a `source` closure ID, resolves the target from `context.codebase`'s static `FunctionLikeMetadata` and discards `signature.return_type`, falling back to `mixed`). In addition, for generator closures containing `yield`, unconditionally overwriting `signature.return_type` with `inner_artifacts.inferred_return_types` clobbers the declared `Generator` return type with `null` or the `return` value type.
trigger: Assigning a closure/arrow function to a variable and calling it (`$a = fn() => 'foo'; $b = $a();` gets `mixed` instead of `'foo'`), or a closure with `yield` and an explicit `: Generator` return type.
match_rule: Identify either (a) that storing the inferred return type only on `TCallable::Signature` causes direct closure invocations (`$a()`) in `function_call.rs` to ignore it and fall back to the un-inferred codebase `FunctionLikeMetadata` (`mixed`), or (b) that overwriting `signature.return_type` with `inferred_return_types` clobbers declared `Generator` return types on closures containing `yield`.
near_misses: Complaining about template-parameterized closures taking the `TCallable::Alias` branch without identifying either the invocation call-site dropping `signature.return_type` or generator `yield` closures having their return type overwritten.
why_findable: The diff stores `inferred_return_type` on `signature.return_type` in `arrow_function.rs` and `closure.rs` without touching `expression/call/function_call.rs` (where `TCallable::Signature` with `source: Some(id)` delegates to `get_function_like_target` which ignores `signature.return_type`), and unconditionally overwrites `signature.return_type` without checking `function_metadata.has_yield`.
notes: Directly tested by `issue_355.php`.

defect: In `PreferEarlyContinueRule`, the autofix unconditionally negates the `if` condition, then only emits `{ continue; }` inside `if let Statement::Block(block) = body.statement`. When the `if` body is a single braceless statement (`if ($x) doSomething();`), the autofix negates `$x` to `!$x` without inserting `{ continue; }`, silently inverting the program's control flow to `if (!$x) doSomething();`.
trigger: Running `prefer-early-continue` autofix on a loop containing a single braceless `if ($cond) doSomething();`.
match_rule: Identify that for a non-block `IfBody::Statement` (`if ($x) stmt;`), the autofix negates the condition but skips inserting `{ continue; }` because it only handles `if let Statement::Block(block) = body.statement`, silently inverting the branch logic.
near_misses: Complaining about operator precedence when negating conditions or formatting of inserted newlines without identifying the missing `else` branch for non-block `IfBody::Statement`.
why_findable: Right in the newly added rule file, `check` matches `IfBody::Statement(body)` with `if let Statement::Block(block) = body.statement` and no `else` branch, immediately after unconditionally emitting condition-negation edits.
notes: Local to `prefer_early_continue.rs` (`relation: false`). Directly tested by `crates/linter/tests/prefer_early_continue.rs`.

defect: 940836000c split short echo tags (`<?= ... ?>`) out of `Statement::OpeningTag(OpeningTag::Echo(...))` into a new `Statement::EchoTag(EchoTag)` AST variant and implemented `Format for EchoTag` in `crates/formatter/src/internal/format/mod.rs`, but missed updating `print_statement_slice` in `crates/formatter/src/internal/format/statement.rs`, which still only checks `if let Statement::OpeningTag(tag) = stmt` to wrap inline PHP tags in `Document::Align` using the line's leading HTML indentation. As a result, multiline `<?= ... ?>` tags inside indented HTML lose their alignment and break to column 0.
trigger: Formatting an indented multiline `<?= ... ?>` short echo tag embedded inside HTML (e.g., inside `<div>` with 4 spaces of indentation).
match_rule: Identify that splitting `OpeningTag::Echo` into a separate `Statement::EchoTag` variant left `print_statement_slice` in `crates/formatter/src/internal/format/statement.rs` matching only `Statement::OpeningTag`, causing indented `<?= ... ?>` tags in inline HTML to miss `Document::Align` indentation.
near_misses: Complaining about `EchoTag::format` wrapping single expressions with `IndentIfBreak` without identifying that `statement.rs::print_statement_slice` was not updated to handle `Statement::EchoTag` for HTML alignment.
why_findable: The diff removes `OpeningTag::Echo` from `Statement::OpeningTag` and adds `Statement::EchoTag`, updating `format/mod.rs` and `comment/format.rs` while leaving `statement.rs:67`'s `if let Statement::OpeningTag(tag) = stmt` HTML-alignment handler untouched.
notes: Directly tested by `issue_1149`.

defect: In `variable_usage.rs`, `walk_foreach` records `fe.target` (`$key => $value`) with `ExprCtx::Write` BEFORE calling `self.rec.enter_arm()`. Because `DeadStoreRecorder::record_write` (consumed by `no_dead_store.rs`) treats any write outside an arm as an unconditional overwrite that kills a preceding pending store, assigning a default value before a `foreach` (e.g., `$child = 0; foreach ($a as $child) { ... } use($child);`) is falsely reported as a dead store — even though when `$a` is empty the `foreach` target is never assigned and the post-loop read observes `0`.
trigger: Linting `$child = 0; foreach ($a as $child) { some($child); } some($child);` with `no-dead-store` enabled.
match_rule: Identify that `walk_foreach` in `variable_usage.rs` emits an unconditional `ExprCtx::Write` for `fe.target` before `enter_arm()` (treating the loop target as always executing), causing `no-dead-store` to falsely flag a pre-loop initialization of the loop variable that is read after the loop when the iterable may be empty (0 iterations).
near_misses: Complaining about `foreach` by-reference `&` bindings or `while`/`for` loop conditions without identifying that `fe.target` is recorded as an unconditional write before `enter_arm()`, falsely clobbering pre-loop assignments when the loop executes 0 times.
why_findable: The diff adds both `walk_foreach` (emitting `ExprCtx::Write` on `fe.target` right before `self.rec.enter_arm()`) and `DeadStoreRecorder` (where writes before `enter_arm()` unconditionally mark prior writes dead, while writes inside an arm do not).
notes: Directly tested by inline `test_lint_success!` tests `foreach_target_does_not_dead_store_pre_loop` and `foreach_key_value_target_does_not_dead_store_pre_loop` in `no_dead_store.rs`.

defect: When assigning `$arr[$dynamicKey] = $val` to a `TKeyedArray`, `29538c8b15` changed `known_items` to `keyed_array.get_known_items().cloned()`, preserving existing known item types verbatim without widening them with `value_type`. Because `$dynamicKey` can alias an existing known key at runtime, the analyzer subsequently assumes `$arr['known']` still has its old type instead of `old_type | value_type`.
trigger: Starting with `$arr = ['a' => 1];`, executing `$arr[$k] = 'str';` where `$k` is `string`, and then reading `$arr['a']` (wrongly typed as `1` instead of `1|'str'`).
match_rule: Identify that `known_items: keyed_array.get_known_items().cloned()` in `update_array_assignment_child_type` fails to widen existing known item value types with `value_type` when a dynamic key may overwrite an existing key.
near_misses: Complaining about `non_empty: true` or list-to-keyed conversion without identifying that cloned `known_items` are not widened with `value_type`.
why_findable: The entire 26-line commit diff replaces overwriting known items with `value_type` by `.cloned()`, visibly dropping any union with `value_type` for keys that `key_type` can match.
notes: Local to `update_array_assignment_child_type` (`relation: false`). Directly tested by `issue_1709.php`.

defect: 350ebe5a0d unwrapped parenthesized bases in `member_access.rs` and added an early `return false` in `parens.rs::called_or_accessed_node_needs_parens` for both `Expression::Binary(_)` and `Expression::Conditional(_)` when `parent_node()` is `PropertyAccess`/`NullSafePropertyAccess`, expecting their dedicated precedence helpers to add parens. While it added a `PropertyAccess` check to `binary_node_needs_parens`, it added NO equivalent check to `conditional_needs_parens` (and `need_parens`'s new `Node::Conditional(_)` guard checks `parent_node()` instead of `nth_parent_kind(2)`, which misses when `PropertyAccess::format` in `format/mod.rs` wraps the object in `Node::Expression` first). Consequently, `($a ?: $b)->value` and `($a ? $b : $c)->value` have their required parentheses stripped into `$a ?: $b->value`, silently changing PHP runtime semantics.
trigger: Formatting `($values->gender ?: Gender::UNKNOWN)->value` or `($a ? $b : $c)->value`.
match_rule: Identify that returning `false` for `Expression::Conditional(_)` in `called_or_accessed_node_needs_parens` when the parent is `PropertyAccess`/`NullSafePropertyAccess` strips required parentheses around ternary/elvis expressions because `conditional_needs_parens` has no `PropertyAccess` check (and `need_parens` checks `parent_node()` for `Node::Conditional` while `Expression::format` sits between `PropertyAccess` and `Conditional`).
near_misses: Complaining about `unwrap_parenthesized` losing comments or `Binary` expressions without identifying that `Expression::Conditional` loses its required parentheses in `PropertyAccess`/`NullSafePropertyAccess`.
why_findable: In the 61-line diff, `called_or_accessed_node_needs_parens` returns `false` for BOTH `Expression::Binary(_) | Expression::Conditional(_)`, while only `binary_node_needs_parens` gets the `nth_parent_kind(2)` check for `PropertyAccess`/`NullSafePropertyAccess` — and `format/mod.rs` + `format/expression.rs` push `Node::Expression` between `PropertyAccess` and `Conditional` so `need_parens`'s `parent_node()` check does not trigger.
notes: Directly tested by `issue_1198`.

defect: In `can_condition_be_initially_false`, `LessThan`/`LessThanOrEqual` match `(left_ub, right_lb)` with `(None, _) => true` and `_ => false`, and `GreaterThan`/`GreaterThanOrEqual` match `(left_lb, right_ub)` with `(_, None) => true` and `_ => false`. When the other side is unbounded (e.g., `$i < $n` with `$i = 0` (`left_ub = Some(0)`) and `$n: int` (`right_lb = None`)), the tuple `(Some(0), None)` falls into `_ => false`, falsely concluding the loop condition can never be initially false (i.e. the loop always enters).
trigger: A loop `for ($i = 0; $i < $n; $i++)` where `$n` is an unbounded `int` (so `right_lb` is `None` and `$n` may be `<= 0`).
match_rule: Identify that `can_condition_be_initially_false` returns `false` when one bound in `(left_ub, right_lb)` or `(left_lb, right_ub)` is `None` (missing `(_, None)` for `<`/`<=` and `(None, _)` for `>`/`>=`), falsely assuming the loop always executes at least once.
near_misses: Complaining about non-integer loop conditions or off-by-one `>=` vs `>` comparisons without identifying the missing `None` wildcard arm.
why_findable: Directly visible in the 20-line match table in `f066934547`: if `right_lb` is `None` (`-inf`), `$a < $b` can clearly be false regardless of `left_ub`, yet `(Some(_), None)` hits `_ => false`.
notes: Local to `can_condition_be_initially_false` (`relation: false`). Directly tested by `issue_1762.php`.

defect: In `Lexer::interpolation`, the buffering loop runs `let subsequent_token = self.advance()?.ok()?;`. When `self.advance()` returns `Some(Err(syntax_error))` (such as a null byte or unexpected character inside a string interpolation), `.ok()?` silently drops the `SyntaxError`, returns `None` (signaling EOF to callers), drops any buffered tokens, and exits without restoring `self.mode` or `self.interpolating`.
trigger: Lexing a double-quoted string containing an invalid byte (e.g. a null byte `\0`) inside an interpolated expression.
match_rule: Identify that `self.advance()?.ok()?` inside `Lexer::interpolation` converts a lexing `Err` into `None` (premature EOF), swallowing the `SyntaxError` and skipping restoration of `self.mode` and `self.interpolating`.
near_misses: Complaining about `VecDeque` allocation or `has_offset(end_offset)` without identifying `self.advance()?.ok()?` dropping `Err` as `None` and failing to restore lexer state.
why_findable: In the diff of `Lexer::interpolation`, `self.advance()?.ok()?` directly discards `Err(SyntaxError)` as `None` before the lines restoring `self.mode` and `self.interpolating`.
notes: Local to `Lexer::interpolation` (`relation: false`). Directly tested in `crates/syntax/tests/tokenizer.rs`.

defect: 617411d16b guarded `all_parameters_match = false` with `if !parameter_comparison_result.type_coerced_from_as_mixed.unwrap_or(false)` without checking the template parameter's variance. Because `union_comparator::is_contained_by` sets `type_coerced_from_as_mixed = Some(true)` when comparing an unparameterized `Box` (`Box<mixed>` from template default) against `Box<resource>`, `generic_comparator::is_contained_by` returns `true` for `Box<mixed>` contained by invariant `Box<resource>`. Callers such as `crates/analyzer/src/utils/docblock.rs` then treat `/** @var Box<resource> $b */ $b = box($seed);` as `RedundantDocblockType` or allow unsound invariant generic coercion.
trigger: An invariant generic `interface Box<T>` where a function returns bare `Box` (`Box<mixed>` from template default) and a caller narrows it with `/** @var Box<resource> $b */ $b = box($seed);` (or passes `Box<mixed>` where invariant `Box<resource>` is required).
match_rule: Identify that suppressing `all_parameters_match = false` when `type_coerced_from_as_mixed` is true in `generic_comparator::is_contained_by` ignores `Variance::Invariant`, treating `Box<mixed>` as contained by `Box<ConcreteType>` (breaking invariant generic checks / causing false `RedundantDocblockType` in callers like `docblock.rs`).
near_misses: Complaining about `from_template_default` flag propagation or sealed class inheritor narrowing in the same commit without identifying that `type_coerced_from_as_mixed` is inappropriately allowing invariant generic parameters to match.
why_findable: In `generic_comparator.rs`, `container_metadata.template_variance.get(parameter_offset)` is checked 10 lines earlier for `Variance::Contravariant`, yet the newly added `if !parameter_comparison_result.type_coerced_from_as_mixed` skips setting `all_parameters_match = false` even for invariant parameters where `union_comparator` sets `type_coerced_from_as_mixed`.
notes: 617411d16b introduced the forward-branch `type_coerced_from_as_mixed` skip (which triggers `issue_1746_invariant_generic_var_with_mixed.php` since `from_template_default` is true); f223d4a9 later copied the same pattern into the reverse branch, and 863b796f fixed both.

defect: When checking whether a concrete class implements an interface's abstract property hook (e.g., `interface I { public string $x { get; } }`), `analyze_class_like` checks `current_property.and_then(|p| p.hooks.get(hook_name)).map(|h| !h.is_abstract).unwrap_or(false)`. In PHP 8.4, a plain concrete property (`public string $x;`, where `p.hooks.is_empty()`) satisfies interface `{ get; }` / `{ set; }` hooks, so requiring an entry in `p.hooks` produces a false-positive `UnimplementedAbstractPropertyHook` error.
trigger: Implementing `interface I { public string $name { get; } }` with `class C implements I { public string $name = ''; }`.
match_rule: Identify that checking `p.hooks.get(hook_name)` rejects plain concrete properties (`p.hooks.is_empty()`) implementing interface abstract property hooks, emitting a false `UnimplementedAbstractPropertyHook` error.
near_misses: Complaining about property hook population (#45) or visibility asymmetry without identifying that a plain concrete property without explicit hooks satisfies interface property hooks.
why_findable: Directly visible in `analyze_class_like` in `e294ce2a48` where `p.hooks.get(hook_name)` returns `None` -> `false` for any ordinary non-hooked property.
notes: Local to `analyze_class_like` (`relation: false`). Shares `intro_commit` e294ce2a48 with #45 (not counted toward the 25 distinct relation diffs).

defect: `expand_alias` binds the RAII cycle-detection guard with `let _ = AliasExpansionGuard::new(class_name, alias_name);`. In Rust, `let _ = expr;` drops the temporary immediately at the semicolon before `expand_union(...)` executes, so `AliasExpansionGuard::drop` immediately removes `(class_name, alias_name)` from `EXPANDING_ALIASES`, completely disabling cycle detection and causing a stack overflow on any recursive type alias.
trigger: Expanding a self-referential type alias such as `/** @phpstan-type SelfRef = int|array<int, SelfRef> */`.
match_rule: Identify that `let _ = AliasExpansionGuard::new(...)` drops the RAII guard immediately instead of holding it across the recursive `expand_union` call (needs a named binding like `let _guard = ...`), disabling cycle detection and causing infinite recursion / stack overflow.
near_misses: Complaining about `RefCell` borrow panics or `HashSet` seeding without identifying the immediate drop caused by `let _ =`.
why_findable: Line 547 literally writes `let _ = AliasExpansionGuard::new(class_name, alias_name);` right before `expand_union(...)`, while `AliasExpansionGuard`'s `Drop` impl is added in the same diff 30 lines above.
notes: Local Rust RAII bug inside `expander.rs` (`relation: false`). Directly tested by `test_expand_alias_cycle_detection`.

defect: f4292e32f7 added `IssueCode::DocblockParameterNarrowing` in `add_parameter_types_to_context` whenever a parameter's `@param` docblock drops a branch of its native PHP union type, without checking whether the method overrides a parent/interface method (`context.codebase.method_is_overriding(...)`). Because PHP's LSP signature rules require an overriding method (such as a class implementing a generic interface `KeyedCollection<int<0, max>>`) to keep the parent's wider native union (`int|string $k`) while specializing `@param int<0, max> $k`, the check reports an unfixable error (tightening the native type would be a PHP fatal error).
trigger: `interface KeyedCollection<Tk of array-key> { /** @param Tk $k */ public function at(int|string $k): string; }` implemented by `/** @implements KeyedCollection<int<0, max>> */ class NonNegativeIntVector implements KeyedCollection { /** @param int<0, max> $k */ public function at(int|string $k): string { ... } }`.
match_rule: Identify that the new `DocblockParameterNarrowing` check in `add_parameter_types_to_context` runs on overriding/implementing methods without checking `method_is_overriding`, falsely flagging valid generic interface/parent specializations where PHP forbids narrowing the native parameter union type.
near_misses: Complaining about template type checks (`has_template_types()`) or `atomic_comparator` logic without identifying overriding/implementing methods constrained by parent native signatures.
why_findable: The diff adds `DocblockParameterNarrowing` inside `add_parameter_types_to_context` (which runs for all functions and methods, including overrides whose inherited/specialized docblocks are populated by `codex/src/populator/docblock.rs`) and its own help message tells the user to 'tighten the native type', which violates PHP LSP for overriding methods (tracked by `CodebaseMetadata::method_is_overriding`).
notes: Fixed 17 minutes later in 96edb0e6 with regression test added to `docblock_parameter_narrowing.php`.

defect: d5d366aec7 modified `split_tag_content` to treat any `&` after whitespace as a type continuation (`found_continuation = next_char == ':' || next_char == '|' || next_char == '&'`) to support multiline intersection types (`Foo & Bar`). However, `split_tag_content` is called by `parse_param_tag` (and `crates/codex/src/scanner/docblock.rs`) on `@param` tags where `&$var` and `&...$vars` denote PHP by-reference parameters, not intersection types. Because `split_tag_content` consumes `&$var` into the type string, `rest_slice` becomes empty and `parse_param_tag` fails with `Missing parameter name`.
trigger: Parsing a docblock with a by-reference `@param` tag such as `@param array<string, mixed> &$data` or `@param array<int> &...$arrays`.
match_rule: Identify that treating any `&` after whitespace as a type continuation in `split_tag_content` misparses by-reference `@param` syntax (`&$var` / `&...$var`) consumed by `parse_param_tag`, absorbing the parameter name into the type string and failing to parse the `@param` tag.
near_misses: Complaining about `|` or `:` continuations or bracket nesting without identifying the collision between `&` intersection continuation and by-reference `&$var` / `&...$var` parameter syntax.
why_findable: The diff adds `next_char == '&'` to `split_tag_content` in `crates/docblock/src/tag.rs`, while `parse_param_tag` and `parse_var_ident` in the same file (lines 485-505) call `split_tag_content` expecting `&$var` / `&...$var` to remain in `rest_slice`.
notes: Directly tested by `issue_955.php`.

defect: When a child method overrides a parent method without its own docblock (`!from_docblock`), `inherit_method_docblocks` unconditionally overwrites `child_method.return_type_metadata` with the parent's substituted docblock return type, ignoring `child_method.return_type_declaration_metadata` (the child's native PHP return type recorded by `scanner/function_like.rs`). When a parent has `@return T|null` with native `: ?object` and the child covariantly narrows its native return type to non-nullable `: object`, `inherit_method_docblocks` widens the child's effective return type back to `stdClass|null`, causing false nullable-argument errors at call sites.
trigger: `abstract class Factory<T> { /** @return T|null */ abstract public function create(): ?object; }` extended by `/** @extends Factory<stdClass> */ class UserFactory extends Factory { public function create(): object { return new stdClass(); } }`, then passing `$factory->create()` to `function use_stdclass(stdClass $obj)`.
match_rule: Identify that `inherit_method_docblocks` overwrites `child_method.return_type_metadata` with the parent's inherited docblock return type without narrowing/intersecting against the child's native `return_type_declaration_metadata` (e.g., preserving `|null` from parent even when the child's native return type is non-nullable).
near_misses: Complaining about `@inheritDoc` tag detection in `scanner/function_like.rs` or parameter contravariance without identifying that inherited return types ignore the child's narrower native return type declaration.
why_findable: The diff adds `inherit_method_docblocks` in `populator.rs` overwriting `child_method.return_type_metadata` whenever `!from_docblock`, even though `FunctionLikeMetadata` (populated by `scanner/function_like.rs`) separately holds `return_type_declaration_metadata` which in PHP can covariantly narrow a parent's nullable return type to non-nullable.
notes: Directly tested by `inherited_docblock_narrowing.php`.

defect: In `scrape_special_function_call_assertions`, `9ada332d98` changed the `"in_array"` branch (which already guards on `strict: true`) from `Assertion::IsType(atomic)` to `Assertion::IsEqual(atomic)`. In the reconciler (`crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/assertion_reconciler.rs`), `Assertion::IsEqual` models PHP loose equality (`==`), under which `int` and `float` can loosely equal `string` — whereas `Assertion::IsIdentical` models strict `===`. As a result, `in_array($x, $strings, strict: true)` fails to narrow `float|int|string` to `string`.
trigger: `$requestedLocale` of type `float|int|string` checked with `if (in_array($requestedLocale, ['de', 'en'], strict: true)) { takesString($requestedLocale); }`.
match_rule: Identify that `scrape_special_function_call_assertions` emits loose `Assertion::IsEqual` instead of strict `Assertion::IsIdentical` for `in_array(..., strict: true)`, causing the reconciler to treat the check as loose `==` and fail to narrow away incompatible scalar types (like `int`/`float` against `string`).
near_misses: Complaining about `Psl\Iter\contains` or non-strict `in_array` without identifying that `Assertion::IsEqual` models loose `==` instead of strict `===` (`Assertion::IsIdentical`) for `in_array` with `strict: true`.
why_findable: In `assertion.rs`, the `"in_array"` arm explicitly returns `None` unless `should_strict_check` (`arg 2` is `true`), yet the 4-line diff emits `Assertion::IsEqual(atomic)` instead of `Assertion::IsIdentical(atomic)`, whose loose-equality semantics are defined in `crates/analyzer/src/reconciler/assertion_reconciler.rs`.
notes: Directly tested by `issue_1628.php`.

defect: `FunctionLikeParts::format` calls `f.print_trailing_comments_between_nodes(signature_end, block.left_brace)` BEFORE calling `self.format_signature(f, settings.space_before_params)`, and passes the returned `dangling_comments` to `format_body` to be printed after brace `spacing`. Because `FormatterState::print_trailing_comments_between_nodes` imperatively consumes comments in `[signature_end.end_offset(), block.left_brace.start_offset()]` and advances `self.next_comment_index`, it steals any trailing line comment sitting on the signature line (e.g. `function foo(): bool // @phpstan-ignore`) before `format_signature` (via `wrap!` / `print_trailing_comments`) can emit it on the signature line, relocating the comment onto the opening `{` line under `NextLine` brace style.
trigger: Format a PHP function or method using `NextLine` brace style whose signature ends with a trailing `//` comment on the same line as the return type / parameter list (e.g. `private function f(...): bool // @phpstan-ignore method.unused`).
match_rule: Must connect calling `f.print_trailing_comments_between_nodes(signature_end, block.left_brace)` before `self.format_signature(...)` in `FunctionLikeParts::format` to `FormatterState`'s stateful `next_comment_index` cursor stealing trailing comments on the signature line and moving them into `format_body` after the brace newline.
near_misses: Complaining about `get_signature_end_span` missing `use_clause` or `is_insignificant` whitespace logic without identifying that `print_trailing_comments_between_nodes` runs before `format_signature` and preempts signature trailing comments.
why_findable: The diff adds `print_trailing_comments_between_nodes` advancing `self.next_comment_index` and calls it at line 302 of `function_like.rs` directly above `self.format_signature(f, ...)` at line 307, while `format_signature` formats `return_type_hint` / `parameter_list` through `wrap!` which calls `f.print_trailing_comments` using the same `next_comment_index` cursor.
notes: base = intro^; naive top_blamed was 0b4aec02bd (which had no dangling_comments yet), traced via git log -S dangling_comments to 95ef9dd204.
